name: Vytautas Magnus University
summary: Liberal-arts university in Kaunas with 16 English-taught bachelor's across social sciences, informatics, sciences, business and music.

ib.text: Upload your IB diploma and results (60% average minimum); English at B2 is shown by test or by a school letter that your education was in English. Motivation letter; a maths test or interview may follow.

programmes.name: Economics and Finance
programmes.about: Three-year business economics degree taught entirely in English: economics and finance with computational thinking, teamwork, an internship and a behavioural economics lab.
programmes.overview: Over three years you study microeconomics, macroeconomics, statistics and mathematics, then international economics, econometrics, labour economics, public finance, investment and risk, and financial accounting, with research methods alongside. Teaching draws on practitioners from universities, NGOs and business, and on the faculty's behavioural economics laboratory. Internships are mostly with international companies in Lithuania and abroad, followed by a qualification practice and a bachelor thesis, and you can work towards an international CMA management accounting certificate. Graduates go into finance and strategy roles, public policy work and analytical units, or on to a master's.
programmes.selectionNote: Score is your school-grade average 70% plus motivation letter or interview 30%; at least 60% overall average to apply.

programmes.name: Business Administration
programmes.about: Entrepreneurial leadership and management: how businesses and organisations work, for future managers, consultants and business owners.
programmes.overview: You study microeconomics, macroeconomics, management, finance, marketing and organisational behaviour, then financial reporting, human resources, business law, entrepreneurship, leadership and strategic management. Electives include digital marketing, sales management, lean management, logistics, artificial intelligence and e-sports. Business and public-sector representatives take part in lectures, and practical work comprises term papers, a qualification placement and a bachelor thesis. Graduates move into management, consulting and organisational administration, start their own ventures, or continue to a master's in business administration.
programmes.selectionNote: Score is your school-grade average 70% plus motivation letter or interview 30%; at least 60% overall average to apply.

programmes.name: Logistics and Commerce
programmes.about: Smart, sustainable logistics operations, sales techniques, IT in commerce and building your own e-business.
programmes.overview: After microeconomics, mathematics and business basics, you study logistics management, logistics equipment and technology, e-commerce, warehousing and inventory, transport systems, and customs procedures, with finance, human resources and business law as support. Entrepreneurship training, business planning and market research give practical experience, and the final year brings a professional internship and a bachelor thesis. Partner firms contribute lectures, company visits, traineeships and thesis topics. Graduates work as logistics coordinators, supply chain administrators and transport specialists, in retail and agricultural logistics, or start commerce ventures.
programmes.selectionNote: Score is maths 40%, English 40% and motivation letter or interview 20%.

programmes.name: Sustainable Bio-Business Management
programmes.about: Management, economics and technology for the bioeconomy: running and developing organisations in a changing labour market.
programmes.overview: Early semesters cover mathematics, economics, business law and management basics; later modules combine financial management and marketing with green chemistry, biomaterials, circular economy, agricultural systems, biotechnology and sustainable bioenergy. Two practicums, in semesters five and eight, give workplace training, and a bachelor thesis closes the degree. Partner companies give lectures and offer internships and project topics, and Erasmus+ exchanges are available. Graduates work as managers, project managers, sustainability consultants and marketing or sales specialists in bioeconomy organisations, or in related ministries.
programmes.selectionNote: Score is maths 40%, English 40% and motivation letter or interview 20%.

programmes.name: Political Studies: World Politics and Economy
programmes.about: Global politics, international relations, political economy, economic diplomacy and trade, through topics such as migration, climate change and geopolitics; taught in English.
programmes.overview: The degree joins political science with economics: political systems, global politics, international relations, international political economy, geopolitics, EU politics, human rights and economic diplomacy. Regional courses look at East Asia, Latin America, and US, Russian and EU policy, with attention to the EU's Eastern Partnership. Research methods run alongside, and internships take place at political institutions, international organisations, companies and diplomatic missions, before a bachelor thesis. Graduates work as policy advisers, diplomats and researchers, including in foreign ministries, or continue to a master's.
programmes.selectionNote: Score is a history, geography, economics or IT grade 30%, English 30%, motivation letter 30% and maths 10%.

family.name: Political Studies
family.differs: Focus on global politics, international political economy and trade.
family.cardLine: Global politics, political economy and trade

programmes.name: Political Studies: International Politics and Development Studies
programmes.about: Developing regions, international processes, human rights, migration and development strategy, preparing political analysts who compare and explain political and economic change.
programmes.overview: You study political systems, international relations, development studies, colonialism and post-colonialism, human rights, comparative politics, international economics and conflict resolution in developing countries. Regional courses focus on the post-Soviet states and the Middle East and North Africa, and you add a regional language at B1 level, chosen from French, Spanish, Arabic, Russian or Turkish. Internships take place in political institutions, international organisations and diplomatic missions, followed by a bachelor thesis. Graduates work in government, research institutes and international organisations, or go on to a political science master's.
programmes.selectionNote: Score is a history, geography, economics or IT grade 30%, English 30%, motivation letter 30% and maths 10%.

family.name: Political Studies
family.differs: Focus on developing regions, human rights and development strategy.

programmes.name: Sociology and Anthropology: Society, Culture and Communication
programmes.about: Sociology with a communication specialisation: researching and forecasting social processes and communicating them to the public, taught in English.
programmes.overview: The degree pairs classical and contemporary sociological thinking with communication: public relations, strategic communication, visual communication and international communication. Topic courses cover religion, crime and social control, gender, ethnicity and nationalism, migration and family diversity, and you learn qualitative and quantitative methods. Practical work includes two in-service trainings, a creative production lab, an engaged journalism lab and a bachelor thesis, with Erasmus+ and bilateral exchanges available. Graduates work as analysts and communication specialists in media, advertising, market research, human rights organisations, think tanks and ministries.
programmes.selectionNote: Score is history 40%, maths 40% and English 20%.

programmes.name: English Philology
programmes.about: English linguistics, discourse and philology for careers in teaching, translation, computational linguistics and media; taught entirely in English.
programmes.overview: You study English phonetics, linguistics, morphology and syntax alongside British, American and Canadian literature, translation strategies and language teaching methodology. Practical elements include career-planning training, translation practice, corpus analysis and a qualifying teaching practice. Electives cover semantics and pragmatics, sociolinguistics, literature and media, and American and British civilisation. The programme works with schools, translation agencies, language course providers and international companies. Graduates become translators, interpreters and English teachers, work in banks, businesses and EU organisations, or go on to master's and doctoral study.
programmes.selectionNote: Score is your average of school exams 80% plus an English grade 20% (B2 minimum).

needs.note: B2 minimum; counts 20% of the score

programmes.name: Biology and Genetics
programmes.about: Biology foundations and genetics, for careers in biotechnology, biopharmaceutics, the food industry and environmental protection.
programmes.overview: You study general biology, physics and chemistry, then invertebrate and vertebrate biology, morphophysiology, microbiology, biochemistry, general and molecular genetics and immunology, and later biophysics, cell cultures, ecological genomics, epigenetics and neurobiology. Teaching includes laboratory courses, field work in plant and animal biology, term papers and a bachelor thesis, with internships chosen in companies and institutions linked to the programme. Electives range from beekeeping and forest entomology to aquaculture systems and ecogenotoxicology. Graduates work in biotechnology, biopharmaceutics, the food industry, environmental protection, health care and forensics, or continue to a master's or doctorate.
programmes.selectionNote: Score is English 20%, maths 20%, biology or chemistry 30% and motivation letter 30%. Some places are state-funded.

programmes.name: Biotechnology
programmes.about: Laboratory work and data analysis with modern methods, plus IT skills to develop biotechnology products for pharmaceutics, environment and industry.
programmes.overview: The first semesters cover general biology, chemistry, biotechnology and mathematics, then organic chemistry, physics and genetics, followed by biochemistry, immunology, cell cultures, enzymology, bioinformatics, omic technologies and AI in biotechnology. Teaching centres on laboratory work with modern equipment, two internship periods with partners such as Thermo Fisher Scientific, and a bachelor thesis. Partner companies help shape the curriculum and give guest lectures, and electives include fermentation technologies and food biotechnology. Graduates work in research laboratories, biopharmaceutical and food industries, cosmetics or environmental agencies, or continue to a master's.
programmes.selectionNote: Score is English 20%, maths 20%, biology or chemistry 30% and motivation letter 30%. Some places are state-funded.

programmes.name: Informatics Systems
programmes.about: Information systems and networks, programming, data analysis and visualisation, with specialisations in software systems, AI systems or business informatics.
programmes.overview: You start with mathematics, programming, discrete structures and object-oriented programming, then graphics and visualisation, computer architecture, databases, human-computer interaction, networks, Java, software engineering, internet technology and AI applications. From there you follow one of three tracks: software systems (mobile, IoT and cloud), artificial intelligence systems, or business informatics. Teaching combines labs, applied research with industry partners, term papers, a final-year practicum under a mentor and a bachelor thesis. Graduates work as software developers, architects, data analysts and project managers in start-ups and government, or continue to a master's in informatics or computer engineering.
programmes.selectionNote: Score is maths 40%, English 30% and motivation letter 30%.

programmes.name: Multimedia and Internet Technologies
programmes.about: Images, video and audio together with programming, graphic design and internet technology, for people who like both mathematics and art.
programmes.overview: Mathematics, programming, databases, computer architecture and networks sit beside audiovisual art, visual communication, composition and digital sound. Later modules cover programming virtual environments and computer games, graphics and visualisation, augmented reality, AI in games, interactive multimedia and animation, and web graphics design. Teachers and students work with multimedia, creative-industry and game-development firms, and the final semester combines an internship with the bachelor thesis. Graduates work in game development, 3D modelling, animation, virtual reality, web design and creative technology, or continue to a master's in Lithuania or abroad.
programmes.selectionNote: Score is maths 40%, English 30% and motivation letter 30%.

programmes.name: Sustainable Engineering
programmes.about: Digital engineering for biological systems: production technologies, robots and drones, combining engineering with computer science and environmental care.
programmes.overview: You begin with chemistry, mathematics, physics, engineering graphics, mechanics, biology and programming, then thermodynamics, electronics, agronomy, fluid mechanics, machine elements and computer-aided design. Later courses cover environmental engineering, mechatronic systems, AI and machine learning, robotics and drones in agriculture, bio-waste recovery, circular economy and data science. Teaching includes laboratories and a semester-long engineering design practice, and more than forty companies equip labs and contribute to courses. Graduates work as engineers, technologists and managers in agricultural modernisation, food production, waste management and bioenergy, or continue to a master's.
programmes.selectionNote: Score is maths 40%, English 30% and motivation letter 30%.

programmes.name: Music Production
programmes.about: Sound recording and design, music marketing and music technology, with creative projects of your own and the link between sound and visuals.
programmes.overview: You study sound engineering, sound recording basics and technologies, sound recording design, applied music production, composition, and music marketing and project management, with a thread of audiovisual art linking sound to video, photography and graphic design. Teaching is project-based and uses three professional recording studios, with video and multimedia projects, a music production practice in the final semester and a bachelor thesis. The whole programme is taught in English. Graduates work as audio specialists, sound directors for television, radio and theatre, music producers, sound artists and managers in music organisations, or continue to study abroad.
programmes.selectionNote: Score is a written test 50%, portfolio 30% and an interview 20%.

programmes.name: Performing Arts
programmes.about: Classical and jazz performance as a soloist, ensemble musician or conductor, with music history and theory, pedagogy and research at the VMU Music Academy.
programmes.overview: Individual instrument or voice study sits beside ensemble work in chamber groups, orchestras, jazz ensembles and vocal groups through all eight semesters, with an opera studio, soloist practice and music event practice. Theory covers solfeggio, harmony, polyphony and composition, with music history from the Middle Ages to the 21st century and teaching methods for choirs. You choose one of eight tracks: accordion, choir conducting, jazz, piano, strings, vocal, wind and percussion, or popular music, and finish with a final art project in that track. Erasmus+ exchanges are available. Graduates perform in orchestras, ensembles, theatre and opera, teach, or continue to a master's.
programmes.selectionNote: Score is an entrance exam and video recording 70% plus an interview 30%; English at B1 is also asked.
programmes.ib: Audition by entrance exam and video recording; English at B1.

programmes.name: Sports Studies (in Kaunas)
programmes.about: Coach education for all sports, based on the American Sport Education Program, with modern training methods and technologies.
programmes.overview: The first year covers functional anatomy, motor control, sports genetics, biomechanics, physiology and medicine, and biochemistry and nutrition, followed by three levels of coaching theory and didactics and the theory and practice of a chosen sport, plus sports psychology and testing in sport, with attention to AI and e-sports. Coaching practice runs over three semesters, with internships in sports centres in Lithuania or abroad and a partnership with Kaunas Zalgiris basketball club. Optional tracks lead to international certificates, for example in athletic training or personal training. Research methods and a thesis finish the degree. Graduates work as coaches, athletic trainers, competition officials and sports managers.
programmes.selectionNote: Score is sports achievements and motivation interview 40%, your school-grade average 40% and English 20%.

notes: EU/EFTA citizens pay a lower fee than other students (for example €3,250 against €3,400); it is the standard fee set by the Lithuanian ministry, and you pay the full first year in one instalment after you are accepted.
Applications for the 2027-28 autumn intake open in the beginning of November 2026, and studies start on 23 August 2027 (preliminary); the 2027 rules are still to be published.
Accounting and Finance is left out: its first year is taught in Ukrainian or Russian. Biology and Genetics and Biotechnology are marked as having state-funded places.
